stem: Johnny is a 10-year-old boy who has been thrown from his bike, was knocked unconscious, and is arriving by ambulance as a semi-conscious trauma patient. What is the best order for his initial assessment in the emergency department?

options.text: Breathing> Airway with Cervical Spine control> Circulation with haemorrhage control> Disability or neurological status> Exposure
Disability or neurological status> Exposure> Airway with Cervical Spine control > Breathing> Circulation with haemorrhage control
Airway with Cervical Spine control> Breathing> Circulation with haemorrhage control> Disability or neurological status> Exposure
Exposure> Disability or neurological status> Breathing> Airway with Cervical Spine control> Circulation with haemorrhage control
Disability or neurological status> Exposure> Breathing> Airway with Cervical Spine control > Circulation with haemorrhage control

explanation: The primary survey in paediatric trauma follows the ABCDE approach: Airway with cervical spine protection, Breathing, Circulation with haemorrhage control, Disability, then Exposure. This sequence prioritises immediate threats to life and helps prevent secondary brain injury by ensuring oxygenation and perfusion.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: This is a standard paediatric trauma primary survey question. The correct sequence is ABCDE, which is option C.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect: breathing is assessed after airway protection in the ABCDE sequence.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect: disability and exposure come later in the primary survey.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: this is the standard ABCDE order for initial trauma assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect: exposure should be last, after immediate life-threatening issues are addressed.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect: disability is important, but it is not assessed before airway, breathing, and circulation.

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
